newsitem.title: UK: Palmoil ends lower, soft oils trim gains in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Palmoil ends lower, soft oils trim gains in Europe.

text.p: Palm oil prices ended the week lower on the European vegetable oil market as Malaysian output pressure built up again.
Forecaster Ivan Wong's estimate of higher output and stocks itself had little impact on prices but talk of an increase over and above Wong's figures made European traders cautious.

Wong put local palm oil production at 801,000 tonnes during August, up 11 percent over July. End-August stocks were estimated at 775,000 tonnes against 754,634 at end-July while exports were put at 680,000 tonnes against 646,017 tonnes.
Traders noted talk that Malaysia's Oil Palm Growers Council may come up with a bigger production figure.
"Wong is talking of an 11 percent increase but figures as high as 15 to 17 percent are being mentioned," said a trader.
"With these sort of numbers being bandied about most people are going to wait for the official PORLA figures on Monday before they do anything," said another trader.
News that India's State Trading Corp (STC) had purchased one parcel of palm olein for October 5-20 shipment at $582 a tonne c and f had little effect on a quiet pre-weekend market.
This is the STC's second purchase this week - it bought 12,000 tonnes of olein on Tuesday.
Crude palm oil cif Europe closed unchanged to $2.50 down while refined palm oils were unchanged to $5 lower.
Coconut oil finished unchanged to $2.50 up after Sep/Oct traded at $730 a tonne cif, while palmkernel oil was $5 lower in a neglected market.

Lower Chicago futures trimmed sellers' prices at the close in Europe with soy oil ending the session unchanged to 0.50 guilders up and rape oil 0.75 to 1.50 guilders higher. --Jim Ballantyne, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8062
